trust_decision.summary: Decided in UserResourceImpl's read handlers: before any identity lookup the caller must both be allowed to administer the requested realm and that realm must actually contain the requested user; the fix adds throwIfCannotReadUserInRealm (throwIfCannotAdminRealm plus isUserInRealm) to get/getUserClientRoles/getUserRealmRoles/getUserSessions and throwIfCannotAdminRealm to getClientRoles, because every provider lookup underneath is realm-blind.

landing_point.why: The advisory names UserResourceImpl and GET /user/{realm}/{userId} is the route that hands a request-supplied realm plus a request-supplied user id straight to a realm-blind getUser(userId) and returns the whole User (email, name, attributes, enabled) to a READ_ADMIN of another realm.

fix_sites.module_kind: JAX-RS resource over the MQTT connection store (manager module)

fix_sites.entry_point: GET /user/{realm}/{clientId}/roles (UserResource.getClientRoles) - role catalogue, no user id, previously guarded only by @RolesAllowed
n/a - shared guard throwIfCannotReadUserInRealm called by every read route

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The SPI lookup the routes call is realm-blind by contract - getUser(String userId) takes no realm and internal services (AlarmService:261, LocalizedNotificationHandler:172) rely on resolving ids outside any request realm - so a solver can argue the realm decision is not the provider's job and the advisory names only UserResourceImpl.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A non-admin authenticated user must still read their own record and roles (the self branch at UserResourceImpl.java:105 and the getCurrent family), and a realm admin holding only READ_ADMIN must still read other users of its own realm - reusing the write-side helper throwIfNotSameRealm would wrongly demand WRITE_ADMIN, so the fix adds a separate read helper, which is also why its test setup has to grant READ_ADMIN to the realm admin user (fix.diff:101-111).

O6_input_shapes: realm path param naming a foreign realm (e.g. master) while the caller is an admin of another realm
own realm path param carrying a userId that belongs to another realm
realm plus clientId only, with no user id at all (getClientRoles role catalogue)
current-user routes whose realm comes from the Realm request header rather than the path
superuser cross-realm access, which must keep succeeding

O8_uncovered_routes.route: GET /user/{realm}/disconnect/{sessionID} -> disconnectUserSession never looks at the realm and has no admin check, so any authenticated caller can force-disconnect a session given its broker connection id
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: the session id is an opaque broker connection id and the realm segment is unused in the lookup, so 'realm is meaningless here' reads as intentional, and the advisory is about reading user data rather than acting on sessions
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, one method below the getUserSessions sink the fix closes

O8_uncovered_routes.route: PUT /user/{realm}/userRoles/{userId}/{clientId} and PUT /user/{realm}/userRealmRoles/{userId} -> updateUserClientRoles/updateUserRealmRoles check only throwIfCannotAdminRealm and never isUserInRealm, so the write twin of the same user-identity decision stays open
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: the advisory describes disclosure and these are writes, and the Keycloak provider scopes its user lookup by realm so a foreign userId merely 404s - defensive only
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, write routes on the opposite side of the class from the reads the fix changed

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a throwIfCannotWriteUserInRealm guard on updateUserClientRoles and updateUserRealmRoles
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: both routes already take (realm, userId) and already carry an admin-realm check, so a maintainer adding the read-side helper would plausibly add its write twin in the same change.
it sits beside getUserSessions and shares the same broker connection store, and the project's own test file already asserts admin-realm rejection on every other user route.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: realm/user scoping of READ_ADMIN notification queries that take realmId and userId query params
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: same shape (READ_ADMIN annotation plus caller-supplied realmId/userId) and the same 'Only the superuser can call this operation' javadoc assumption, but in another package - a maintainer could copy the pattern there.

O9_family: CWE-639 authorization bypass through a user-controlled key: missing cross-realm scoping on user, role and session reads (broken object-level authorization)

O10_build.toolchain: Gradle wrapper 9.5.1; sourceCompatibility and targetCompatibility 21 at project.gradle:391-392
O10_build.project_tests: test/src/test/groovy/org/openremote/test/users/UserResourceTest.groovy - a Spock spec that starts the manager container in-process but authenticates against a live Keycloak and reads users from PostgreSQL; the pinned tree already has realm-admin tests for the write routes (e.g. 'Update user realm roles requires realm administration rights' at :418) and none for the read routes.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a realm-admin check to the four read methods only, reusing throwIfNotSameRealm (which demands WRITE_ADMIN) and comparing the stored realmId to the path realm, which happens to match only for the master realm.

out_of_scope_notes: NotificationResourceImpl:64-95 (outside this advisory): READ_ADMIN notification queries take realmId and userId with no realm check despite the javadoc 'Only the superuser can call this operation'; noted only, not pursued.

AlarmService:261 and LocalizedNotificationHandler:172,177 call the realm-blind ManagerIdentityProvider.getUser with ids from other subsystems rather than directly user-controlled path params; noted only, not pursued.
unverified: Only the advisory summary string was provided (no GHSA body), so the trust decision is derived from the summary plus the fix diff and the pinned code.
No latest release was supplied, so present_in_latest for the O8 routes is unknown.
Repository size in MB could not be measured without a shell, so tiny_repo/giant_repo were not evaluated.

Whether the grading harness can start PostgreSQL and Keycloak (profile/dev-testing.yml) for hidden tests is unknown; the project's own suite requires them, which makes the verification loop heavier than the fix itself.
MQTT and websocket transports were not searched for a second route into the user-identity sink.
